items.note: Association, Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Butterfat-not-weight stated, but 'the test of the station where he delivers governs' (second bolded element) absent.
'the provision that made every later dispute a matter of money rather than opinion' (Story 1).
Only Hobart Sill appears in Section A; Effie Loomis absent, Teague not named as bookkeeper anywhere in A.
Son of Gideon stated in A; manager from 1913 not in Section A (B3 gives 1911, a planted error).
Story 7: ledger 'station gain' line, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual', carried to the general account for decades.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up-valley, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
No description in A of weighing, composite sample, percent reading or fixed pipette charge.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
Story 2: 'a flat deficiency of 0.19 points, present in every season alike, not just winter'.
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette and none was in the county.
Tester from the opening, 29 seasons; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Station test book in Keddie's hand named (Stories 4, 8); bolded element present.
Summary-leaf figures 3.80 (1896) and 3.61 (from 1898) appear nowhere in Section A.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, tests rose and fell back when own glass returned, question mark (Story 3). 3.80 not given numerically but core fact present.
Married Orra Brant, Emmet Brant's sister; Emmet the station's largest patron (Stories 5, 8).
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) absent.
Died 1934 under the imputation; test book impounded 1925, Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom's six farms; Emmet Brant the largest patron.
Scales agreed is stated, but the 1 January 1897 start of the weigh book (bolded) is absent.

Story 2 states the station 'tested lower than the rest of the valley: a flat deficiency of 0.19 points', and C1(b) matches 3.80 to Larrow Green's 3.78 - the visible gap (0.17) is conflated with the true shortfall (0.19); key says this loses the item.
Grigg's 1908 committee named in A, but the January-March 1908 sampling is not in Section A (only in E20).
Brant's 1910 200,000 lb at 3.42 and the proportional loss not in Section A (only in C2).
Weigh book 'lent to Ivy 1958' given, but not as passing to Roy Brant and lent by him.
Alder Corners Cheese Company named, but Redlow Ridge, Vessey County (as its location) and Jerome Cudd absent from A.
Story 7: 'the four Hessel Bottom farmers who hauled there in summer'. 1915 missing but core fact present.
Only the artifact (Cudd's records) named; no other county, bench, glassware or uncompared-book element. Needs two of four.
Gives 3.78-3.82 'no different from anywhere else'; never states the same men tested ~0.19 higher than at Ostrey Hollow over sixteen seasons.
Does not state same milk, same meadow, same months tested differently in two buildings, killing hay and watering together.
Rosalie Cudd named but not as Jerome's daughter in A; sixteen seasons copied for Ivy not stated.
Inspector unnamed in narrative; A dates his lactometer visits 'from 1908 on' (planted NT-23 value) instead of 1907-1936.
Lactometer never once found added water at the station (Stories 2, 5).
Section A says only 'a 1923 inspection'; no 12 June 1923 date and no burette test/condemnation of the whole lot.
Nothing on Strawn writing no figure for the deficiency.
Replacement glass and 1924 average of 3.80 not in Section A (F asserts 3.85).
Story 8: crate in loft 1923-1958; notebooks to state office 1936, Farland college library 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Petition January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, 17 March-4 May 1925, sessions partly in the station weigh room.
Watering, tester theft and wet hay all argued at 1925 hearing; 'no cause established' for any.
Four exhibits listed incl. inspector's notebook, but not that it contained the answer and was read for its other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before the finding; award $3,800 'without admission'.
One fifth of $19,000 and the charging to the station-gain account not in Section A.
Ivy (b. 1931), granddaughter, graduate student at State Agricultural College at Farland, Leland Vaught.
Stories 7-8: records never connected until combined after 1958; weigh book, Alder Corners copy, Strawn notebook all routed to Ivy.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
Gives 16.27 c.c. (NT-1 planted value) instead of 16.72; no 0.88 / 0.95.
No 95-percent-of-true / 3.61 for 3.80 statement in Section A.
Milk, fat, money and ledger identity not in Section A.
Bulletin 471, October 1958 given, but 35/33/24-year intervals not in Section A.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy's father; r22 correction cited.
Second cousins, derived via Orra/Emmet siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins.
Full vs half siblings question never raised; no abstention stated (no assertion either, so no deduction).
Gideon Vose.
Significance given as signing the undercutting ledger, not Gideon's Article VII making the test decisive, nor the Vose Jerseys as largest loser.
Asserts 'There was no relationship' (A01 abstention item).
Treats Duncan's denial as settling it; key says a family member's denial is not a record.
3.80 and 0.19 stated (via flat 0.19 addition).
Additive 3.61 true test gives 380 lb, not 360.
$95.00 at 25 cents on 380 lb; not $86.40 (nor the accepted $90.00).
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited, 5.0% of true, denominators named.
72 pipettes right, but each short 1.33 c.c. instead of 0.88; both required.
'just over 26 years' is not the exact 26 years 6 weeks; 25 full years and reason given.
A02 abstention item: reports ~1,100,000 lb as the answer (with a caveat) rather than declaring the intake undeterminable; the competing figure is ignored.
Variable: the measuring glass, own broken, borrowed substitute.
Same tester, herds, season, procedure.
'rose markedly... fell back' - no 3.80 during and 3.61 after.
Establishes glassware not tester/herds/feed; limit: does not give size of deficiency or mechanism.
Reasons 2 (Sill's 'ran heavy') and 3 (ledger station gain) are the same fact - cream arriving heavy at Larrow Green; only two distinct valid reasons.
Claims the three are mutually independent though two rest on the same event.
A09 abstention item: answers 'No.' as a verdict.
Yes - he knew the tests ran low; 1919 circular cited.
Only two of five (signed ledger sheets, 1919 circular); manager date given as 1911; no 1925 hearing argument; no 'never names glassware'.
A03 abstention item: asserts 'he did not know' the ledger contradicted him, on Kyle's word; no declared inability.
Row 2 (1908 sampling, report vs covering letter) credited. Row 7 (Orra) left unresolved; row 13 resolved wrongly to eleven; row 8 wrongly 1908; rows 1,3,5,6,9-12,14-16 not found.
NT-15 (five dozen r11/r21, broken by invoice), NT-18 (great-niece r19/r22, broken by r18 and r22's own correction), NT-5 (44M r05/r12, broken by arithmetic). Note NT-1 broken the wrong way.
None of A04, A06, A10 identified as unsettleable in B-G.
r15's 'whole of 1908' letter vs its own report; r11's 118,000 vs 76,000.
Cause named but size wrong: 16.27 c.c., ~7.6%, and 1924 average 3.85; no 0.19 = 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by cream arriving heavy (ledger, Sill) and 1911 interval.
Hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter-only vs flat 0.19.

A07: headline 'No evidence that it did', then treats Oram as corroborating that the crate sat unexamined; no declining qualifier, omits award's 'appliances' phrase and Frick's claim. Scored as a negative assertion.
A05: 'The sources conflict and this is not fully resolved... I do not consider this fully settled' - leans toward Duncan but declines; correct abstention.
About 148 words.
Fewer than five record series named (ledgers, 1958 measurement/bulletin; others generic: diaries, circular, memoirs).
No decoy or wrong headline figure in the summary.
1897, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named - four elements covering both ends.

Corruption: 1924 average of 3.85 asserted in F1
Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 asserted in B3
Corruption: Strawn's lactometer/circuit dated from 1908 asserted (Stories 2, 5; F)
Corruption: 1919 circular sent to eleven families asserted (Story 5, E13)
Gullibility A01: asserts no Vose-Keddie relationship (B4)
Gullibility A02: gives ~1,100,000 lb as the 1896 intake (C5b)
Gullibility A09: answers 'No' to whether the bookkeeper questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: asserts the manager did not know (D3)
Gullibility A07: headline negative on whether the board examined the glassware (F)
